text.p: Sunbeam Corp. said Thursday it has completed most of the cost-cutting initiatives announced in November as part of a restructuring plan to transform the struggling appliance maker.

Excluding personnel and facilities associated with businesses up for sale, Sunbeam said it has already achieved its job-cut targets, exceeded its warehouse reduction targets and closed all but one of the production facilities identified for closure.

Sunbeam, based in Delray Beach, Fla., said in November it would cut 6,000 jobs, or about half of its work force, and eliminate 87 percent of its product lines. The company also said it would reduce the number of production facilities for its ongoing businesses to eight.

The measures were taken about four months after Albert Dunlap became chairman and chief executive, and shortly after Sunbeam reported a third-quarter loss of $28.7 million, or 22 cents per share, as sales fell about 2 percent from the year-ago period to $244.9 million.
"Our goal was to have a dramatically different company in 1997," Dunlap said. "We will now focus our energies on implementing our growth strategy."

The company, whose Sunbeam and Oster brands are household names, said it is now operating nine factories associated with its ongoing businesses. Only the Bay Springs, Miss., location, with fewer than 100 workers, remains to be closed.
Sunbeam said it has already achieved its goal of cutting 6,000 jobs, including about 3,000 employees currently in businesses to be sold.
In the restructuring, Sunbeam also planned to slash its warehouses from 61 to 24. So far, it has already closed 25 warehouses and expects to close four more early this year, it said.
Excluding the 14 warehouses used by businesses to be sold, Sunbeam said it now expects to use 18 warehouses for its ongoing operations, six fewer than previously announced.

In late December, Sunbeam sold its decorative bedding product line to Perfect Fit Corp. The company is in the process of selling businesses associated with other product lines identified in its November announcement -- outdoor furniture, time and temperature and Counsellor and Borg branded scales. Sunbeam expects to sell all of these businesses, including associated plants and equipment and transfer of personnel, during the first quarter.
Sunbeam's stock gained 12.5 cents to $26.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
